title: 02. Ingestion & Chunking: Recursive Character Text Splitting
summary: Recursive Character Text Splitting is LangChain's most versatile and production-recommended chunking strategy.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body:
Recursive Character Text Splitting is LangChain's most versatile and production-recommended chunking strategy. It works by recursively trying a list of separators in priority order: first attempting to split on paragraph breaks (`

`), then line breaks (`
`), then sentences (`. `), then words (` `), and finally individual characters. This means chunks respect semantic boundaries as much as possible given the size constraint — a chunk will never be split mid-sentence if a paragraph boundary exists nearby. It's the default choice for most document types because it handles diverse document structures (technical docs, articles, conversations) without requiring document-specific configuration.

sections.title: ② Key Code
sections.body:
```python
from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
from langchain_core.documents import Document

# Standard production configuration
splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
    chunk_size=512,           # tokens (use TokenTextSplitter wrapper for token-accuracy)
    chunk_overlap=64,         # overlap tokens
    length_function=len,      # character length by default
    separators=[
        "\n\n",   # Paragraph break (highest priority)
        "\n",     # Line break
        ". ",     # Sentence end
        "? ",     # Question end
        "! ",     # Exclamation end
        "; ",     # Semicolon
        ", ",     # Comma
        " ",      # Word boundary
        "",       # Character boundary (last resort)
    ],
    keep_separator=True,
    is_separator_regex=False,
)

# For code files — language-specific separators
from langchain_text_splitters import Language

python_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter.from_language(
    language=Language.PYTHON,
    chunk_size=1000,
    chunk_overlap=100,
)
# Uses Python-aware separators: class, def, \n\n, \n, " ", ""

# For Markdown documents
markdown_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter.from_language(
    language=Language.MARKDOWN,
    chunk_size=512,
    chunk_overlap=64,
)
# Uses: ## headings, \n\n, \n, etc.

# Token-accurate recursive splitting (production recommended)
from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
import tiktoken

def get_token_splitter(
    model: str = "text-embedding-3-large",
    chunk_size: int = 512,
    chunk_overlap: int = 64,
) -> RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter:
    """Create token-aware recursive splitter for a specific model."""
    enc = tiktoken.encoding_for_model(model)
    
    return RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
        chunk_size=chunk_size,
        chunk_overlap=chunk_overlap,
        length_function=lambda text: len(enc.encode(text)),
        separators=["\n\n", "\n", ". ", "? ", "! ", " ", ""],
    )

# Usage
splitter = get_token_splitter(chunk_size=512, chunk_overlap=64)
docs = [Document(page_content="Long document text...", metadata={"source": "doc.pdf"})]
chunks = splitter.split_documents(docs)

# Verify all chunks respect token limit
enc = tiktoken.encoding_for_model("text-embedding-3-large")
for chunk in chunks:
    assert len(enc.encode(chunk.page_content)) <= 512 + 10  # +10 buffer for edge cases
```

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
``` RECURSIVE CHARACTER TEXT SPLITTING — HOW IT WORKS ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ ALGORITHM: Try separators in order until chunk fits ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Document (2000 chars, target chunk_size=500): Step 1: Try "\n\n" (paragraph break) "Section 1\n\nSection 2\n\nSection 3" → Split: ["Section 1", "Section 2", "Section 3"] → Each fits in 500 chars? YES → Done ✓ If Section 2 is 800 chars: Step 2: Try "\n" (line break) on Section 2 → Sub-split Section 2 on lines If a line is still 600 chars: Step 3: Try ". " (sentence) on that line → Sub-split on sentences If a sentence is still 550 chars: Step 4: Try " " (word boundary) → Sub-split on words Last resort: "" (character) → Split at exact character position (avoid if possible) PRIORITY ORDER (highest to lowest boundary quality): ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 1. \n\n ← Best: full paragraph preserved 2. \n ← Good: full line preserved 3. ". " ← OK: full sentence preserved 4. "? " ← OK: full question preserved 5. " " ← Marginal: at least full words 6. "" ← Worst: may cut mid-word SEPARATOR CUSTOMIZATION BY DOCUMENT TYPE: ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Plain text: ["\n\n", "\n", ". ", " ", ""] Markdown: ["## ", "### ", "\n\n", "\n", ". ", " "] Python code: ["class ", "def ", "\n\n", "\n", " ", ""] Legal: ["SECTION ", "Article ", "\n\n", ". ", " "] HTML: ["

", "", "\n", ". ", " "] ```
